best_for: Gaming clans and communities that already run a TeamSpeak 3 server and need the matching client on their Windows or Mac machines.

points.title: Voice chat on servers you control
points.text: TeamSpeak lets you host your own server, so your group decides the settings, permissions and who keeps the logs. People who cannot host can join TeamSpeak's own community servers instead.

points.title: Encryption built in
points.text: TeamSpeak says AES-based encryption is standard, and security can be set per server or per channel. Noise reduction, echo cancellation and a choice of audio codec help on poor mics.

points.title: TeamSpeak 6 sits next door
points.text: The download page now also offers a TeamSpeak 6 client, still in beta at the time of review, for Windows, macOS and Linux. Check which version your server runs before you pick a client.

points.title: The client is free
points.text: The TeamSpeak 3 client is freeware with no subscription. Hosting a server is a separate matter with its own licensing.

points.title: Linux is on the vendor site
points.text: TeamSpeak offers a 64-bit Linux client and Android and iOS apps, but this listing covers Windows and macOS only.

points.title: Per-user or system-wide on Windows
points.text: Installers come in 32-bit and 64-bit, for the current user or for all users, and need Windows 10. The Mac download is a universal build. The Windows listing keeps 5 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
